current_proof_excerpt: 4.1 Under [A3], fix an $r$ for which collision balance holds $\nu$-almost everywhere. The function $(v,w,v',w')\mapsto A-B$ is continuous. If it were nonzero at an allowed collision, it would remain nonzero on a relative open neighborhood; full support of $\nu$ gives that neighborhood positive measure, contradicting balance. Hence balance holds for every elastic collision. The set of such $r$ has full Lebesgue measure and is dense in $\Omega$; continuity in $r$ extends the identity to any limit point when needed. [A1, A3, F1, step 3.1, algebra]
